title: The Subsistence Agrarian Perimeter and Root Cellars
standalone_fallback: If arable soils freeze, flood, or suffer blighted rot, the settlement opens sealed winter root cellars and transitions to parched grain rationing, wild hedgerow foraged turnip soups, and slaughtering non-essential dairy sheep, maintaining subsistence for 30 days before starvation checks begin.

title: The Communal Artesian Well and Village Cistern
standalone_fallback: If the artesian springhead runs dry or suffers surface contamination, the settlement reverts to hand-hauled snowmelt runoff, roof rainwater cisterns, and strict boiling of muddy ditch water, sustaining up to 300 residents at 4 liters/day under mild dysentery risk before migration becomes unavoidable.

title: Vernacular Timber, Wattle & Stone Masonry
standalone_fallback: If timber rot, roof fires, or clay shortages compromise municipal masonry, the community crowds into smoke-choked central longhouses, turf dugouts, and sheep byres; hypothermia and respiratory coughing inflict Light checks during rain, but community cohesion keeps the node habitable without collapse.

title: The Ditch-and-Palisade with Town Watch Bailiff
standalone_fallback: If timber palisades rot or the bailiff's watch dissolves, the hamlet retreats into a central fortified stone church tower or communal barn, barricading doorways with oak tables and sounding brass alarm horns; petty marauders loot outer gardens, but residents survive sieges up to 7 days before surrender.

title: The Weekly Barter Square and Village Blacksmith
standalone_fallback: If iron scrap or charcoal supplies fail, the forge goes cold; the village reverts to wood-pegged plows, stone-sharpened scythes, and pure commodity barter (bushels of oats for wool fleeces); agricultural efficiency drops 30%, but mundane village exchanges continue without monetary currency.

title: The Village Herbalist, Midwife & Leechcraft Hearth
standalone_fallback: If medicinal herbs run out or the midwife dies, the community relies on boiled onion poultices, pine-needle tea, and elder hearth vigils; non-magical disease recovery slows by 50% and infant mortality climbs, but basic domestic care prevents immediate depopulation.

title: The Midden Trenches, Swine Scavengers & Night-Soil Pit
standalone_fallback: If swine die or lime dust runs out, the village digs emergency muck pits 200 yards downwind and covers waste with river gravel and pine ash; foul odors inflict Light morale penalties, but basic separation of waste from wellhead drainage prevents cholera outbreaks.

title: The Wayside Boundary Shrine & Hearth Vigil
standalone_fallback: If the boundary shrine is desecrated or sacred icons are smashed, the community fractures into suspicious family enclaves; solstice feasts cease, paranoia against outsiders spikes, and characters suffer disadvantage on morale checks, but private hearth candle vigils sustain baseline social survival.
